title: How does a plant drink water?

steps.title: How does a plant drink water?

beats.say: Plants get thirsty, just like you! But a plant has no mouth.
So how does it drink? Let's look under the ground!
Here are the roots. They spread out under the soil, like long fingers.
Every root is covered in tiny root hairs.
The root hairs soak up water from the soil, like a sponge.
Then the water travels up the stem, inside thin tubes.
The tubes work like drinking straws. They carry water all the way to the top.
The water spreads into every leaf, through little lines called veins.
Leaves use water, sunlight and air to make food for the plant.
Leaves have tiny holes, too small to see. They are called stomata.
The sun warms the leaf, and some water floats away as invisible vapour.
As water leaves the top, it pulls more water up from the roots, just like sipping through a straw!
So remember. Roots soak it up. The stem carries it. And leaves let it out.
In the Quran, Allah tells us that He made every living thing from water.
beats.caption: Allah made every living thing from water. (Quran 21:30)

beats.say: So go and give a plant a drink today!
